newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Mobutu cronies fled leaving huge electricity bills.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu cronies fled leaving huge electricity bills.

text.p: Members of ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko's regime fled owing $180 million in unpaid electricity bills, state radio reported on Wednesday.
The radio, quoting state power company SNEL, said the bill covered both domestic and industrial consumption -- the latter for factories owned by Mobutu cronies.
It gave no indication of the timeframe over which the bills were accrued.
Over three decades of corruption and chaotic administration under Mobutu left Africa's third largest nation, potentially one of its richest, on its knees.
The former Zaire, renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo, has a wealth of minerals, rich farmland and huge hydro-electric potential.
The radio said that the hole in the accounts was compromising President Laurent Kabila's efforts to electrify all 10 provincial capitals. Kabila's forces toppled Mobutu in May.
